translations.answer: The author clarified that the issue is related to time to first iteration (time-to-first-iteration), not the steady-state ms/step: Newton 0.2.0 approaches 10 minutes on 4096 env, and training starts after that. Upgrading to Newton 1.0.0 Beta 3.0v resolved the startup delay and improved initialization, leading to the maintenance person's closure. The thread did not provide a full time table for before and after, so it can be prioritized to upgrade and re-test, but it cannot be extrapolated to all tasks.
translations.applicability: Applies to Newton 0.2.0 in 4096-env contact tasks; compatibility and actual time-to-first-iteration should be re-measured.
translations.credibility.rationale: Environmental, processing steps, and results have engineering records, but formal cross-validation or independent replication is missing.
translations.details.attempts.0: The author upgraded Newton; engineers compared full, no_contact_consumers, and cached_contact_consumers tasks, and verified on 8192 env synthetic benchmark.
translations.details.diagnostics.0: Distinguish between time-to-first-iteration and steady-state ms/step, and do not use 'scaling slow' description.
translations.details.diagnostics.1: Timed solver.update_contacts, SensorContact.update, and reward/observation managers, and counted sensor.data access per step.
translations.details.effective_fixes.0: Startup delay: upgrade to Newton 1.0.0 Beta 3.0v.
translations.details.effective_fixes.1: Runtime: cache contact tensor per simulation step and reuse in multiple reward/observation terms.
translations.details.environments.1: Runtime benchmark: IsaacLab develop; Newton backend; Linux 5.15; NVIDIA L40; Dexsuite 64–512 env and synthetic 512–8192 env.
translations.details.limits.0: Startup results are from a single task in Newton 0.2.0, with no full benchmark before and after upgrade.
translations.details.limits.1: Runtime testing is not the original author's startup problem, and caching cannot explain the 10 minutes; caching only recycles part of the total steps.
translations.details.outcomes.0: The author reported faster initialization in high environment numbers, and the maintenance person closed it due to the upgrade.
translations.details.outcomes.1: 512 env cache reduced from 16.70 ms to 13.33 ms; 8192 env repeated reading 2.09 ms, and cache reading 0.43 ms.
translations.details.problem_statements.0: Why does Newton 0.2.0 take nearly 10 minutes to start in 4096 env, and does the upgrade resolve it?
translations.details.problem_statements.1: What is the main cost of contact sensor access during training, is it from the Newton core or IsaacLab repeated reading of sensor.data?
translations.details.suspected_causes.0: Startup delay is related to Newton 0.2.0 version, and the author reported it resolved after upgrade.
translations.details.suspected_causes.1: Runtime benchmark shows repeated consumer-side sensor.data updates and materialization are much higher than isolated Newton contact generation.
translations.details.symptoms.0: Newton 0.2.0 + 4096 env + specific contact pairs take nearly 10 minutes to reach first training iteration; startup after that is acceptable.
translations.details.symptoms.1: Multiple reward/observation terms repeat reading contact sensor in the same step, and contact consumer overhead increases with more environments.
translations.source.locator: Issue #5018, author clarification and upgrade result in issuecomment-4188629387; maintenance person closure confirmed in issuecomment-4204879364
translations.source.title: Startup delay and per-step read cost for Newton contact sensors are two separate performance issues.
translations.terms.1: Time to first iteration (首轮迭代时间)
translations.title: Newton 0.2.0 in 4096 contact environments takes nearly 10 minutes to start training; what was confirmed?
